title: Leica GS18 I Visual GNSS Smart Antenna
summary:
The GS18 I is a GNSS smart antenna with Visual Positioning: GNSS, an IMU, and a global-shutter camera in one instrument. Instead of walking the pole to a point you cannot reach, the surveyor measures the point from the imagery and the software solves the position.

It matters where a pole will not go. A roof edge, the far side of a road, a point behind a gate, a corner of a building: measure from the image and carry on. Leica quotes image points at typically 2-4 cm in 2D from 2-10 m, which is well inside survey tolerance for detail and as-built work, and image groups can be processed later in Leica Infinity.

The rest of the instrument is a serious RTK rover: 555 channels, 8 mm + 1 ppm RTK on a single baseline, tilt compensation, and a 4G LTE modem so it works on a correction service as well as a local base.
specs: RTK single baseline: H 8 mm + 1 ppm / V 15 mm + 1 ppm; network RTK H 8 mm + 0.5 ppm / V 15 mm + 0.5 ppm
Tilt-compensated RTK: additional H uncertainty under 2 mm + 0.3 mm/degree down to 30 degrees tilt
Static long observations: H 3 mm + 0.1 ppm / V 3.5 mm + 0.4 ppm
1.2 MP global-shutter camera, 80 degrees H x 60 degrees V, 20 Hz video; image groups captured at 2 Hz up to 60 s per group
Image point measurement typically 2-4 cm (2D) at 2-10 m
1.25 kg, 173 x 173 x 109 mm; Li-ion 2.8 Ah / 11.1 V, up to 8 h
IP66 with camera / IP68, operating -30 to +50 degrees C
accessories: Leica TS13 robotic total station for a hybrid GNSS and total station setup: the total station tracks a prism on the antenna
Battery charger and spare Li-ion battery
Field controller for capture and export
